The main takeaway from our work is that

the collision energy dependence of elliptic flow at fixed transverse momentum p_T is a sensitive probe of the fluid's shear viscosity, which can be used to discriminate between different initial conditions and different values of the specific shear viscosity.

the collision energy dependence of elliptic flow in the range sqrt(s)=7-2760 A Gev is very weak and can be reproduced with a small specific shear-viscosity eta/s = 1/12 pi, which is consistent with the value obtained from lattice QCD calculations.

the elliptic flow of charged hadrons at midrapidity in heavy-ion collisions is a very robust observable, which can be used as a reference to test hydrodynamical models at the RHIC BES program, and to study the QCD matter created at the LHC.
